children: Indian shares are expected to open higher on Monday, extending a four-week winning streak, as foreign investors continued to buy stocks in Asia's third-largest economy amid easing oil prices and a global selloff in AI-linked stocks.
GIFT Nifty futures (GIFc1) were at 25,912 points, as of 7:58 a.m. IST, indicating a positive start for the benchmark Nifty 50 index

Foreign investors net bought Indian shares worth 103.08 billion rupees ($1.11 billion) on Friday, as per provisional data. They have invested a record $13 billion so far in November, reducing year-to-date outflows to $18.4 billion.
MSCI's broadest index for Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) was down 1% with South Korean equities
trading 3% lower, as investors questioned the massive, largely debt-funded spending on data centres to power AI models.

India's Nifty 50 has surged nearly 12% this month, compared with a 10% decline in MSCI's regional index, as global investors rotated out of AI stocks and returned to Indian equities after two years of selling.

The rally has also been supported by bullish calls from global brokerage firms HSBC and Goldman Sachs, both of which upgraded Indian equities to "outperform" as funds shifted away from global AI stocks.

"Following the sharp, largely uninterrupted rally in recent sessions, the market's ability to withstand deteriorating global risk appetite and defend key support levels will be critical in determining whether the uptrend retains momentum or gives way to profit-booking," said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money.
